subject: Community Preservation Act Project Funding
overview: The City Council approved over $1 million in Community Preservation Act funding for several municipal improvements and received a detailed report from the Health Director on COVID-19 surge mitigation and vaccine rollout plans. The Council also addressed administrative transparency regarding city spending and considered changes to public hearing procedures.

items.title: Pole Grant of Location: Mitchell Avenue
items.summary: Approved a joint petition from National Grid and Verizon to install a new pole near 93 Mitchell Avenue to accommodate a new residential construction, subject to standard engineering and sidewalk repair conditions.

items.title: COVID-19 Mitigation and Vaccine Update
items.summary: Health Director MaryAnn O'Connor provided a briefing on the post-Thanksgiving case surge and the regional plan to begin first responder vaccinations in January; the report was placed on file.

items.title: Ceremonial Recognition: Medford Community Media
items.summary: Approved resolutions congratulating Patrick Gordon and Kat Darnell of Medford Community Media for receiving an overall excellence award from the Alliance for Community Media.

items.title: Request for City Warrant Articles
items.summary: Approved a resolution requiring the administration to provide monthly warrant articles and a FOIA request for 2020 spending records to increase fiscal transparency.

items.title: Special Permit Procedure Review
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting current procedures for special permit applications be filed for committee review to evaluate potential rule updates.

items.title: Proposed Public Hearing Rule Amendment
items.summary: Referred a proposal to the Rules Committee that would require petitioners to present before public comment and establish a mandatory six-day written comment period before a final vote.

items.title: Proposed Eviction Moratorium
items.summary: The President ruled a resolution for a local eviction moratorium out of order because a similar matter remains pending in the Housing Subcommittee. Residents and representatives from the NAACP and Alpha Tenant Union spoke during public participation to urge immediate executive action on the matter.

items.title: Community Preservation Act Funding Appropriations
items.summary: Approved approximately $1.06 million in CPA funds for projects including Brooks Estate restoration, library exterior improvements, playground resurfacing, and the rehabilitation of Tufts Pool and Duggar Park tennis courts.

items.title: Committee Reports and Meeting Schedule
items.summary: Approved the Committee of the Whole report on CPA funding and voted to cancel the regular meeting scheduled for December 29, 2020.
